author: Horsley, John

author: Borghesi, Bartolomeo
title: Career of L. Barbuleius Ligarianus (ILS 1066)

evidence: Ligarianus (cos. 135) as ex-tribune of IX; absence of IX from the Nomina legionum (ILS 2288).

author: Mommsen, Theodor
title: Römische Geschichte V: Die Provinzen von Caesar bis Diocletian = The Provinces of the Roman Empire (tr. Dickson 1886)
ref: RG V (Berlin 1885/6) 171 with n. 2; Provinces I (1886) 191
position_place: Britain: annihilated in a surprise attack on the camp at Eburacum during a Brigantian revolt
evidence: York building stone of 108 (CIL VII 241 = RIB 665) as terminus post quem; replacement by VI Victrix; Fronto (Naber p. 217), SHA Hadr. 5.2, Juvenal 14.196 read as a revolt.
quote: Unter Hadrian ist eine schwere Katastrophe hier eingetreten, allem Anschein nach ein Überfall des Lagers von Eburacum und die Vernichtung der dort stehenden Legion, derselben neunten, die im Boudiccakrieg so unglücklich gefochten hatte. | Dickson: Under Hadrian a severe disaster occurred here, to all appearance a sudden attack on the camp of Eburacum, and the annihilation of the legion stationed there, the same 9th legion which had fought so unsuccessfully in the war with Boudicca.

author: Weber, Wilhelm
title: Untersuchungen zur Geschichte des Kaisers Hadrianus; CAH XI ch. 8
position_place: Britain: destroyed in its camp at Eburacum by rebellious Britons
position_date: revolt crushed by 119; expeditio Britannica ended 119
evidence: Britannia coinage; Fronto; SHA; dating of the expeditio Britannica to 119.
verified_online: partial (quoted in E. Birley 1948/1953, 25 and Campbell 2010, 50)

author: Haverfield, Francis
title: The Roman Occupation of Britain (Ford Lectures, ed. G. Macdonald)
position_place: Britain: annihilated at York in a northern rising
evidence: As Mommsen; VI Victrix supplied by Hadrian; Hadrian's visit 122.

author: Collingwood, R.G.

evidence: Disappearance from history; replacement by VI Victrix under Hadrian; Agricola's forts overrun.

author: Collingwood, R.G. & Myres, J.N.L.

Campbell 2010, 50-1)

author: Parker, H.M.D.

author: Richmond, Ian A.

quote: That the legion was cashiered, there is no doubt, and it seems evident that this fate, at the hands of the disciplinarian Hadrian, followed an ignominious defeat. But the unit was not annihilated.

author: Sutcliff, Rosemary
title: The Eagle of the Ninth (novel)

verified_online: yes (foreword quoted in Campbell 2010, 51 and on rosemarysutcliff.net; Reading Museum page read)

author: Birley, Eric
title: Britain after Agricola and the end of the Ninth Legion
ref: Durham University Journal June 1948, 78-83 = Roman Britain and the Roman Army (Kendal 1953) 20-30

quote: we have been unable to reach a firm conclusion as to the fate of the legion ... the one thing that is reasonably clear is that the traditional view of the disaster to it in the year or two before 120 cannot be maintained.

author: Birley, Eric

Whether the Ninth Legion met its end in Hadrian's Jewish War, or with the ill-fated Severianus at Elegeia in 161, or somewhere entirely different, we can only hope that further epigraphic discoveries will bring clarity

author: Campbell, Duncan B.
